sections.text: Those who thus hate Me, who are cruel, the dregs of mankind, I condemn them to a continuous, miserable and godless rebirth.
So reborn, they spend life after life, enveloped in delusion. And they never reach Me, O Prince, but degenerate into still lower forms of life.
The gates of hell are three: lust, wrath and avarice. They destroy the Self. Avoid them.

So we had been discussing chapter 16, Deva Asurasampatvibhaga yoga. Yoga of Differentiation between the divine and Devilish Estates. These are the two types of qualities we have acquired in this world, going through the various experiences throughout our life. And when we look at it from our perspective, for many lives, weve been going through many different experiences. These experiences leave impressions on my mind. Those impressions create tendencies.
Those tendencies which I have is my wealth. Thats all I carry around from one life to another. All other wealth which I consider my wealth right now is temporary and I have to leave behind. But this wealth which my tendencies I carry with me. So thats my permanent wealth, my permanent portfolio. So Bhagavan said that in that portfolio you may have divine qualities or divine tendencies and also devilish tendencies.
Put simply: positive tendencies and negative tendencies. Positive, as we always know, is helpful. Negative, as we always know, is harmful. So these divine tendencies which I have are liberating. Bhagavan said in the beginning of the chapter, these are liberating tendencies. These tendencies will lead me to act in a manner which will liberate me from my limitations.
Limitations are the ones which are binding me to sorrows and unhappiness. If I were powerful enough to own every piece of real estate in this town, then obviously I wont be competing for buying a house in Twin Hickory because I own everything. But because I am never infinite, this limitedness creates competitions and failures, and that creates sorrows and unhappiness. So were going to say that these divine tendencies which you have acquired through your experiences, which align you more with your own self, are liberating from this bondage -- the bondage of identification with this body, mind and intellect, this limited self which I have right now considered to be my true self. On the other hand, there is the devilish tendency.
Now in this case, even though the word devilish or diabolical sounds too negative, but they are basically tendencies born out of my ignorance. What is the truth about my own Self. So I come to the conclusion that there is no higher self. There is no one to control anything. Whatever I can do, I am by myself. Whatever I need, I need to do to get happiness.
That type of belief will lead me to do things which are only for the sense gratification. These creates the negative tendencies and binds me more and more to this limited self. Bhagawan said these tendencies are binding which are in our normal term. We call it a materialistic view of the world and materialistic approach to life. That this material will give me happiness. The things which I acquire from this world, things which I accomplish in this world will make me happy is the materialistic viewpoint.
The spiritual viewpoint is: if I can be happy by myself, then I really dont need anything external to make me happy. Everything else may be just to fulfill my needs, but not wants. So the desire to sustain myself is not unhealthy. But when that desire becomes an obsession for something, then it becomes unhealthy. As we know, everything in moderation is good. Even obsession to not do something can become very dangerous sometimes.
So Bhagavan described these tendencies and said that these are the tendencies you should avoid. These are tendencies you should try to cultivate in yourself. And then he came to the last topic. He initially said that we have talked about divine qualities a lot. Well talk about these devilish qualities in detail. Thats what we need to pay attention to. As I said in the beginning, our mind has a tendency to only see the divine in us.
Divine qualities in us. Devilish qualities in others. Very easy to see what other people are doing wrong. Very difficult to see what I am doing wrong. We always enhance our resumes. We ask somebody to do his own self evaluation in the end of the year.
If you see his self-evaluation, there is no negative in it, period. His supervisor will find negatives in it. It is very important that we develop the discipline to introspect and find what is not right within my own thinking and negate them. Bhagavan says, these tendencies -- you must know these devilish tendencies. When you detect them in you, remove them so that you can move forward in your life.
Your goal is to be happy. These tendencies will never make you happy. Even though it may seem that they will make me happy, they eventually make you unhappy -- and therefore avoid them. So you have seen that Bhagavan described what an asuric person looks like: Ahankaram Balam Darpam Kamam Krodham Cha Samshritah.
They are full of ego, power, self-conceit, lust and anger. Now we all have all of that in some degree. But if all of them together are powerful, then you become an Asura. If all five of them are at full capacity, then you become an Asura. Mam Atma Para Deheshu Pradvisanto Abhyasuyakah -- they hate my presence in them and in others. In other words, they have no value for life.
They will have no value of life, of their own or others. They will have no value for any noble act or have no desire or to appreciate other people. So they have no knowledge about what is divine in them or their own conscience. They will suppress their own conscience when it is trying to guide them for a right actions. And they will also not recognize the good intentions of others around them when others are trying to help them. These people will hate me in their own body and also in the others.
Tan Aham Dvishatah Kruran Samsareshu Naradhaman Kshipami Ajasram Ashubhan. To these cruel doers, the lowest of men -- as I said, when you are qualified for this distinction, when all five of those qualities are fully developed in you, there is no room for any divine tendency. Then Bhagavan says, I send them to the lowest of the yonis. And we have discussed last time: it is not that Bhagavan is punishing.
So Bhagavan is not sitting there and punishing people. Because you are not doing this right, your own actions will lead you towards the lower and lower state of existence. Whatever the tendency you develop, that is the environment you will feel comfortable. My tendency is to come to Gita class. I will feel comfortable here and somebody may be comfortable doing something else. Because their tendencies.
If your tendency leads you down to this path of the Hankara, Balam, Darpam, Kamam Krudam, you will be born into the same environment again. If you consider this sense gratification is the only goal of life then obviously you will be only seeking that environment. And Bhagawan said, I, as the lawgiver and law enforcement forcer in this world put them into the lowest yoni again and again. Asurim Yonim Apanna Muda Janmani Janmani. Birth after birth, having born in the demonic wombs. Because thats the path I have chosen.
Whatever path I take, I become good at that. So you start your career in engineering or architecture, medicine. You do the first project and the second project and in a short time youll have a huge portfolio of work you do. And suddenly, whether you like it or not, you become an expert in that. And other people say, but you are only expert in this. We can give you work in this field because you only do this.
Thats how we become all experts in something. Because we continue to do the same thing over and over again in the same line of work or same line of actions. So these people are now becoming expert in asuric existence. Ashram yuni mapanna by taking birth in Ashram yuni again and again. Mama aprapyevakantoya tatoyati Adhamam gatim. They continue their existing without attaining me, Attaining me.
By not recognizing their own self. They continue their existence from one life to another without recognizing what is divine in them, without recognizing the sanctity of life. And yantim adamam gatim. And they continue to go lower and lower and lower. Because thats the path they are pursuing, they are progressing into. Then he says, trivedam naraka sidham dwaram.
So up till now we have just discussed what the divine qualities are, what the devilish qualities are, who are divine, who are devilish. But what is the cause? This verse gives us the cause and also the prescription for how to avoid them. Trividham Narakasya Idam Dvaram Nashanam Atmanah. These three are the gates of hell, which are the destroyers of the self. Kamah, Krodhah, Tatha Lobhah -- lust, anger and greed.
These are the only three things which you have to avoid, Bhagawan. Now knowing this, we fall prey to these three. Because how the karma works is once you start thinking about some object. When you constantly think about any object, you develop attachment to it. Then you create a desire for that. If you dont get that object, youre a krodha.
So you created attachment. That attachment became lust. Lust in a sense, I ought to have it. Without that, life is not worth living. So that becomes a kamaha. A normal desire to buy a car is not a kamah because I need it for transportation.
But it becomes obsessed and I have to have BMW and then BMW, BMW, BMW. Then its a problem if I dont get it. Because I said I can buy BMW in $50,000. And then by the time I accumulate 50,000, the car has gone to 60,000 or 70,000. It almost is slightly above my pay grade. And that will make me angry.
So Bhagawan said, thats the mechanism of lust. A normal desire is Innocent. Im thirsty, I need water. I have a desire to drink water. Ill get up, get a glass of water and Im done with it. But a constant obsession about something becomes karma.
When that obsession is obstructed by this world for me to attain that I become angry. So that Krodha, we all learned in chapter two the anger. It shuts down my buddhi. Because we have this safety mechanism just like the breaker trips and electricity that to protect integrity of your mind and intellect. The intellect will shut off so it doesnt overburden. So you have no access to your buddhi.
Your memory bank is completely out of your reach. So you cannot access your wisdom when youre angry. Therefore people say, well I, I did it because I was angry. That means its not appropriate. But I did it because I was angry. So all my actions within the state of anger are actually not really good for me.
We all know that Bhagawan said so avoid karma so you dont have to get angry with Crowther. Thats the second gate of and now what happens is if I have a lust for something or karma for something and I achieve that object easily then become greedy. I have the one time Ive got it done. I buy a lotto for the first time and I get a hundred dollar prize. Well, looks like this is an easy pass. So I do it again and again.
Maybe I can win a jackpot. So that success actually became problem for me. Because I now crave to get that experience again and again and again. When I fail at that, Ill be angry again. So at the end of the day I was nothing but angry. If I get what I want, I still will be angry.
And if I dont get what I want, I still will be angry. So I live in the hell all the time.

Verses 19-20 describe the consequence of persistent demonic tendencies: birth after birth in environments that reinforce those same qualities. This is not divine punishment but natural law - whatever tendencies we cultivate, we become expert in; whatever path we follow, we continue along. Just as a person who builds a career in one field becomes increasingly specialized in that domain, someone who practices cruelty, hatred, and delusion becomes increasingly skilled at those patterns. The teaching warns that such souls, never recognizing their divine nature (mam aprapya), sink to lower and lower states (adhamam gatim). Examine your own expertise: What patterns have you become increasingly skilled at through repetition? Are they patterns that liberate or bind? Today, consciously interrupt one negative pattern before it runs its usual course.
Verse 21 offers the most practical guidance in this chapter: Trividham narakasya idam dvaram - there are three gates to hell: kama (lust/obsessive desire), krodha (anger), and lobha (greed). These three are the root destroyers of the Self. Notice how they interconnect: desire, when obstructed, becomes anger; desire, when fulfilled, becomes greed for more. The cycle is self-perpetuating. Krishnas prescription is simple: tasmad etat trayam tyajet - therefore, abandon these three. Today, keep a mental note each time you feel the pull of obsessive wanting, the heat of anger, or the grasping of greed. Do not judge yourself - simply observe. At days end, review: Which gate did I approach most often? What triggered it? What would it mean to turn away from that gate rather than enter?
